module_title: History of Economic Planning in India (Pre-Independence)
introduction: The Planning Commission did not just appear out of nowhere in 1950. Since the 1930s, Indian scholars and industrialists had been proposing 'blueprints' for the nation's development. We must memorize these historical plans and their authors.

core_concepts.title: Visvesvaraya Plan (1934)
core_concepts.description: The very first attempt at economic planning in India was made by the legendary engineer M. Visvesvaraya. In his book, 'Planned Economy for India', he proposed a 10-year plan with a massive focus on 'Industrialization' (shifting labor from agriculture to industries).

core_concepts.title: National Planning Committee (1938)
core_concepts.description: Formed during the 'Haripura Session' of the Indian National Congress (President: Subhas Chandra Bose). 'Jawaharlal Nehru' was made the Chairman of this committee. (Its final report was heavily delayed due to World War II).

core_concepts.title: Bombay Plan (1944)
core_concepts.description: Officially titled 'A Brief Memorandum Outlining a Plan of Economic Development for India'. It was presented by 8 leading 'Industrialists' of Bombay, including J.R.D. Tata and G.D. Birla. Its goal was rapid economic growth through state intervention and basic industries.

core_concepts.title: Gandhian Plan (1944) & People's Plan (1945)
core_concepts.description:
1. Gandhian Plan: Drafted by 'Shriman Narayan Agarwal'. It strongly opposed heavy industrialization and focused on agriculture and cottage/village industries. 
2. People's Plan: Drafted by the radical leftist leader 'M.N. Roy'. It was based on Marxist socialism and prioritized both agriculture and consumer goods industries.

core_concepts.title: Sarvodaya Plan (1950)
core_concepts.description: Drafted by the great socialist leader 'Jayaprakash Narayan' (JP). It was heavily inspired by the Gandhian Plan and Vinoba Bhave's Sarvodaya idea. It emphasized agriculture, decentralization of power, and small-scale industries.

important_entities.name: M.N. Roy
important_entities.significance: M.N. Roy was a pioneer of the communist movement in India. His People's Plan was a distinctively leftist vision that prioritized providing basic needs to the citizens over creating capitalist monopolies.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A common exam trap: 'The Bombay Plan was drafted by the British Government.' This is FALSE. It was an independent draft created entirely by India's top 'Private Industrialists'.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Narayan for Gandhi, Roy for People, JP for All (Sarvodaya)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Gandhian = Shriman Narayan. People's = M.N. Roy. Sarvodaya = Jayaprakash Narayan (JP).

exam_strategy_tips: 'Match the Following' questions dominate this section. You must be able to perfectly match the year (1934, 1944, 1945, 1950) with the name of the Plan and its Author.
